landing.quickStartText: Choose what feels strangely familiar. Your past-life archetype appears instantly at the end.

footer.aboutTitle: About This Past Life Personality Quiz
footer.aboutText: This Past Life Personality Quiz is designed for entertainment and self-reflection. It does not claim to identify a real past life, prove reincarnation, reveal a factual identity, or provide spiritual, psychological, medical, legal, or professional advice. Results are playful archetype profiles based on your choices.
footer.topicText: Past-life themes in this quiz are fictional and symbolic. They are meant to create a fun sense of mystery, recognition, and imagination, not to make factual claims about your personal history.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Oracle.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by prophecy, pattern-reading, and destiny. The Oracle notices what others miss and trusts the quiet pull of meaning before proof arrives.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Healer.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by tenderness, repair, and emotional care. The Healer carries calm into wounded places and knows that small acts of kindness can change a life.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Warrior.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by courage, conflict, and protection through action. The Warrior moves when the moment asks for bravery and stands firm when others hesitate.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Scholar.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by knowledge, archives, and disciplined thought. The Scholar searches for truth patiently and believes every mystery has a structure waiting to be understood.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Artist.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by beauty, emotion, and creative expression. The Artist turns feeling into form and leaves traces of the heart wherever they go.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Ruler.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by authority, responsibility, and command. The Ruler understands pressure, makes hard choices, and carries the weight of leading others.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Explorer.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by freedom, distant places, and movement. The Explorer is drawn toward horizons, unfamiliar roads, and the feeling that life begins just beyond the map.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Guardian.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by loyalty, duty, and keeping others safe. The Guardian watches the door, remembers promises, and protects what love has placed in their care.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Mystic.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by ritual, hidden worlds, and spiritual pull. The Mystic feels the unseen as a presence nearby and follows symbols where ordinary explanations stop.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Rebel.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by defiance, independence, and broken rules. The Rebel challenges old walls, speaks when silence is expected, and chooses freedom over approval.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Storyteller.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by memory, myth, voice, and human connection. The Storyteller keeps names alive and turns ordinary events into meaning people can carry.

profiles.title: Your past-life archetype is The Inventor.
profiles.copy: Your answers point to a past-life archetype shaped by imagination, cleverness, and making what did not exist. The Inventor sees problems as invitations and trusts the strange spark of a new idea.

stageGroups.title: First Instincts
stageGroups.encouragement: Your first instincts are already opening the old door.

questions.prompt: When you enter a room, what do you notice first?
choices: The mood no one has said aloud
Who seems hurt or uneasy
Where the exits and risks are
questions.explanation: First attention often reveals the role that feels natural to you.

questions.prompt: What kind of pressure brings out your best self?
choices: A puzzle that needs careful study
A blank page that needs beauty
A group that needs direction
questions.explanation: Pressure can show whether you organize ideas, feelings, or people.

questions.prompt: Which path would you choose without overthinking?
choices: A road leaving the city
A gate you promised to watch
A candlelit room full of symbols
questions.explanation: Instant choices can carry the feeling of an older pattern.

questions.prompt: Which role feels natural even without experience?
choices: Questioning a rule everyone accepts
Holding a crowd with a story
Building a tool from spare parts
questions.explanation: Some roles feel familiar before they are learned.

questions.prompt: What kind of compliment would stay with you?
choices: You saw what was coming
You made me feel whole again
You were brave when it mattered
questions.explanation: The praise we remember often names the gift we value most.

questions.prompt: What do you trust first?
choices: Evidence gathered over time
The emotional truth of a moment
The responsibility you have accepted
questions.explanation: Trust can reveal whether your inner compass is mental, emotional, or duty-led.

stageGroups.title: Strange Familiarity
stageGroups.encouragement: Those familiar feelings are becoming more specific.

questions.prompt: Which place feels strangely familiar?
choices: A quiet library with high windows
A coastline under a restless sky
A guarded stone doorway at dusk
questions.explanation: Places that feel familiar can hint at the atmosphere your imagination returns to.

questions.prompt: What kind of dream stays with you?
choices: A temple lit by small flames
A locked room you refuse to obey
A village listening as you speak
questions.explanation: Recurring dream-feelings often point toward a symbolic role.

questions.prompt: Which object would you keep if you found it in an old chest?
choices: A brass instrument with moving pieces
A sealed letter with a warning
A bundle of healing herbs
questions.explanation: The object you save suggests the kind of power you are drawn to protect.

questions.prompt: Which sound feels like it belongs to another life?
choices: Distant drums before a march
Ink scratching across paper
A brush moving over canvas
questions.explanation: Sounds can carry roles: action, study, or creation.

questions.prompt: Which scene gives you an odd sense of recognition?
choices: A throne room before a difficult decision
A map spread under candlelight
A courtyard where you keep watch
questions.explanation: Recognition can appear through setting, duty, and emotional pressure.

questions.prompt: What kind of story always draws you in?
choices: A secret ritual no one understands
A person who breaks a cruel tradition
A voice that saves memories from being lost
questions.explanation: The stories that pull you close often mirror an inner archetype.

stageGroups.title: Your Old-World Role
stageGroups.encouragement: Your old-world role is starting to take shape.

questions.prompt: In an old village, where would people look for you?
choices: Near the stars and omens
Where someone was recovering
At the wall when danger came
questions.explanation: The place others seek you says what they believe you can provide.

questions.prompt: What would your hands be known for?
choices: Copying, measuring, and preserving knowledge
Making color, music, or beautiful objects
Signing orders and settling disputes
questions.explanation: Hands can symbolize study, creation, or authority.

questions.prompt: What task would you accept without complaint?
choices: Carrying news across a dangerous road
Guarding a sleeping household
Preparing a ritual before sunrise
questions.explanation: The task you accept shows the responsibility that feels meaningful.

questions.prompt: What would make people whisper about you?
choices: You challenged the council
You remembered every family story
You built something no one had seen
questions.explanation: Whispers often follow people who change the emotional weather of a place.

questions.prompt: What kind of work would feel sacred?
choices: Reading signs before a journey
Helping someone survive grief
Standing between danger and the weak
questions.explanation: Sacred work is the work you would treat as more than a task.

questions.prompt: Which old role would you secretly enjoy?
choices: Keeper of forbidden books
Painter of royal portraits
Advisor with the final word
questions.explanation: Enjoyment reveals the kind of influence you would choose.

stageGroups.title: Love And Loyalty
stageGroups.encouragement: Your bonds and loyalties are shaping the result.

questions.prompt: What would make you cross a dangerous distance?
choices: A mystery calling from far away
A promise you made to protect someone
A sign you believe must be followed
questions.explanation: Distance feels worth it when it serves freedom, duty, or meaning.

questions.prompt: How would you protect someone you love?
choices: By breaking the rule that traps them
By telling their story so no one forgets
By creating a solution no one expected
questions.explanation: Protection can be defiant, emotional, or brilliantly practical.

questions.prompt: What kind of bond feels deepest to you?
choices: A bond built on shared destiny
A bond built on quiet care
A bond tested by courage
questions.explanation: The deepest bond often reflects what you believe love requires.

questions.prompt: What would you leave behind for someone?
choices: A journal full of guidance
A song, painting, or handmade token
A protected home and clear inheritance
questions.explanation: Legacy can be knowledge, beauty, or structure.

questions.prompt: Who would you trust with your secret?
choices: A traveler who understands distance
A loyal watcher who says little
A quiet ritual-keeper
questions.explanation: Trust often goes to the person whose silence has the right shape.

questions.prompt: What kind of loyalty feels most like you?
choices: Loyalty to freedom
Loyalty to memory
Loyalty to a better future
questions.explanation: Loyalty can belong to a person, an idea, or what has not been built yet.

stageGroups.title: Conflict And Courage
stageGroups.encouragement: The way you face conflict is revealing a sharper outline.

questions.prompt: When conflict rises, what do you do first?
choices: Read the hidden pattern
Calm the person in pain
Step forward before fear spreads
questions.explanation: Conflict shows whether you seek meaning, repair, or action first.

questions.prompt: What weapon would suit you symbolically?
choices: A book of laws and histories
A banner that inspires people
A seal that carries authority
questions.explanation: Symbolic weapons show how you influence others.

questions.prompt: What frightens you the least?
choices: Unknown roads
Long nights on watch
Entering a place others call haunted
questions.explanation: What you can face calmly points toward your old courage.

questions.prompt: What would you risk your reputation for?
choices: Saying the forbidden truth
Protecting a story people want erased
Testing an invention that might fail
questions.explanation: Reputation becomes less important when your deeper role is activated.

questions.prompt: Which kind of battle feels familiar?
choices: A battle of fate and timing
A battle to save someone from harm
A battle fought with real danger nearby
questions.explanation: The battle that feels familiar can reveal what kind of courage you carry.

questions.prompt: Which conflict would you be best at solving?
choices: A dispute over records and truth
A community losing hope
A leader forced to choose
questions.explanation: Problem-solving style can point toward your older social function.

stageGroups.title: Gifts And Talents
stageGroups.encouragement: Your gifts are becoming hard to ignore.

questions.prompt: Which skill would return fastest if you woke in another century?
choices: Finding your way by landmarks
Keeping watch through the night
Reading meaning into symbols
questions.explanation: A skill that feels natural can carry the emotional mark of an archetype.

questions.prompt: What talent would people underestimate in you?
choices: Your ability to resist pressure
Your ability to hold attention
Your ability to improve broken things
questions.explanation: Underestimated talents often become the ones that define a person.

questions.prompt: Which gift feels most like a responsibility?
choices: Sensing what may happen next
Helping people feel safe enough to heal
Acting when no one else will
questions.explanation: Some gifts feel less like talents and more like duties.

questions.prompt: What would you study for years?
choices: Ancient languages and hidden records
Music, color, or human emotion
The art of leading people well
questions.explanation: Long study reveals the subject your inner life keeps returning to.

questions.prompt: What could you do for hours without noticing time?
choices: Planning a route into the unknown
Making sure everything is secure
Preparing a space for quiet reflection
questions.explanation: Losing track of time often reveals the work that absorbs you most.

questions.prompt: Which gift would change your community most?
choices: A fearless challenge to unfair rules
A story that gives people courage
A device that makes life easier
questions.explanation: Community-changing gifts can be disruptive, emotional, or practical.

stageGroups.title: Dreams And Symbols
stageGroups.encouragement: Dreams and symbols are pulling the result into focus.

questions.prompt: Which symbol feels strangely personal?
choices: A silver moon over water
A wrapped hand held gently
A sword resting beside a doorway
questions.explanation: Symbols feel personal when they touch a hidden association.

questions.prompt: What kind of dream would you write down immediately?
choices: A room full of unread books
A painting that seemed alive
A crown too heavy to wear
questions.explanation: The dream you preserve says what image has emotional force for you.

questions.prompt: Which image feels like a memory, even if it cannot be one?
choices: A ship leaving before dawn
A lantern kept burning in a window
A circle of candles on stone
questions.explanation: Images that feel memory-like often carry recognition and mystery.

questions.prompt: What kind of dream stays with you after waking?
choices: Running from a rule you refuse to follow
Telling a story to people around a fire
Solving a machine no one understands
questions.explanation: Dreams that linger often reveal the emotional role you return to.

questions.prompt: Which omen would you take seriously?
choices: The same sign appearing three times
A stranger asking for help
A sudden call to defend someone
questions.explanation: The omen you notice shows what kind of meaning your mind prioritizes.

questions.prompt: Which hidden room would you enter first?
choices: The archive
The music room
The council chamber
questions.explanation: The room you enter points to knowledge, expression, or authority.

stageGroups.title: Power And Purpose
stageGroups.encouragement: Your sense of purpose is giving the archetype its name.

questions.prompt: What kind of freedom would matter most?
choices: Freedom to travel beyond borders
Freedom to keep loved ones safe
Freedom to seek hidden truth
questions.explanation: Freedom means different things depending on what you feel born to protect.

questions.prompt: How would you use influence?
choices: To overturn what is unjust
To preserve stories people need
To build a better method
questions.explanation: Influence reveals whether your purpose is resistance, memory, or invention.

questions.prompt: What would people come to you for?
choices: Guidance before a difficult choice
Comfort after a painful loss
Courage before a hard fight
questions.explanation: What people seek from you points toward the gift they believe you carry.

questions.prompt: What kind of power would you respect?
choices: Power earned through wisdom
Power expressed through beauty
Power used with discipline
questions.explanation: The power you respect reveals the kind you would try to wield responsibly.

questions.prompt: Which mission feels worth a lifetime?
choices: Seeing the world before it changes
Protecting a place that matters
Understanding what lies beyond ordinary life
questions.explanation: A lifetime mission often speaks directly to an archetype.

questions.prompt: What would you want your name attached to?
choices: A brave act of refusal
A legend people still repeat
An invention that changes daily life
questions.explanation: The legacy you imagine shows the purpose that feels most alive.

stageGroups.title: The Life You Left Behind
stageGroups.encouragement: The life you left behind is becoming easier to imagine.

questions.prompt: If you left suddenly, what would remain behind?
choices: A warning no one understood yet
A room where people felt cared for
A shield, scarred from use
questions.explanation: What remains behind can reveal what mattered most in the imagined life.

questions.prompt: What would someone find in your old desk?
choices: Careful notes and copied maps
Sketches, songs, or fragments of color
Letters about decisions and duties
questions.explanation: A desk can hold the residue of study, creativity, or command.

questions.prompt: What would make you leave home?
choices: A road you could not stop imagining
A person who needed your protection
A mystery that felt spiritually important
questions.explanation: The reason you leave reveals what is stronger than comfort.

questions.prompt: What would people argue about after you were gone?
choices: Whether you were dangerous or brave
Whether your stories were true
Whether your idea was genius or madness
questions.explanation: The argument you leave behind shows the kind of impact you made.

questions.prompt: Which unfinished task would haunt you most?
choices: A sign you did not explain
A person you could not save
A fight you could not finish
questions.explanation: Unfinished tasks show the emotional weight your archetype carries.

questions.prompt: What would your old home be remembered for?
choices: A shelf of rare books
A wall covered in beautiful work
A seat where serious choices were made
questions.explanation: A remembered home turns private identity into visible legacy.

questions.prompt: Which final image feels most like yours?
choices: A road disappearing into fog
A lantern held beside a doorway
A star chart beside a bowl of water
questions.explanation: Final images often gather the whole emotional pattern into one scene.

questions.prompt: Which ending would feel most satisfying?
choices: A rule broken so others can breathe
A story carried safely into the future
A creation working for the first time
questions.explanation: The ending that satisfies you shows what kind of change feels meaningful.

questions.prompt: If someone sensed your old self, what would they feel?
choices: A strange certainty about fate
A gentle warmth after pain
A fierce will to protect
questions.explanation: The feeling others sense can be the clearest sign of an archetype.

questions.prompt: What kind of mark would you leave on history?
choices: Knowledge preserved through danger
Beauty that outlives the maker
Order created from chaos
questions.explanation: History remembers people through what they preserve, create, or command.

questions.prompt: Which pull feels strongest right now?
choices: To go farther than before
To protect what is precious
To understand the hidden meaning
questions.explanation: The strongest pull often names the energy you recognize most clearly.

questions.prompt: Which role feels closest to you?
choices: The one who refused to obey
The one whose words survived
The one who invented the impossible
questions.explanation: The role that feels closest reveals the identity that feels most emotionally charged.
